text: In a rectangular park measuring 50 m × 40 m, a company plans to construct a rectangular swimming pool in the middle, surrounded by a uniform-width grass strip throughout the park. Find the dimensions of the swimming pool if the area of the grassy strip is 1184 m².

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Quadratic Equations; formation and solution from an area condition
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q32
meta.extractiveQuote: In a rectangular park measuring 50 m × 40 m, a company plans to construct a rectangular swimming pool in the middle, surrounded by a uniform-width grass strip throughout the park. Find the dimensions of the swimming pool if the area of the grassy strip is 1184 m².

text: Let x m be the uniform width of the grass strip. Then the pool dimensions are (50 − 2x) m by (40 − 2x) m. The area of the park minus the pool area is 1184 m²: 50×40 − (50 − 2x)(40 − 2x) = 1184, giving x² − 45x + 296 = 0 = (x − 8)(x − 37). Reject x = 37 because it makes the pool dimensions negative; x = 8. Therefore the pool is 50 − 16 = 34 m long and 40 − 16 = 24 m wide.

text: Carbon forms millions of compounds whereas silicon, which is just below it in the Periodic Table, forms a few compounds. Explain the reason for the difference in their ability to form compounds.

meta.subject: science
conceptTags: Carbon and its compounds; catenation; atomic size and bond strength
meta.heading: Science (086) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q25
meta.extractiveQuote: Carbon forms millions of compounds whereas silicon, which is just below it in the Periodic Table, forms a few compounds. Explain the reason for the difference in their ability to form compounds.

text: Carbon forms millions of compounds because its small atomic size allows it to form strong, stable C–C bonds and show extensive catenation. Silicon has a larger atomic size and forms weaker Si–Si bonds, so it cannot show catenation to the same extent and forms fewer compounds.

text: (B) 60°. The circumference is 2π(60/π)=120 cm. A 20 cm arc subtends 20/120 of a full turn, so the central angle is 60°.

Reason (R): For any event E, if P(E) = 1, then E is called a sure event.

(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
